title: Unit Distance!?
statementMd:
Construct a set of n points in the Euclidean plane such that:

- The absolute values of both coordinates of every point are at most 105;
- Each coordinate of every point becomes an integer when multiplied by 1013;
- The distance between any two points is at least 10−4;
- At least ⌊12nlog2n−n⌋ distinct unordered pairs of points have distance in [1−10−9,1+10−9].

## Input

The first line contains an integer T (1≤T≤100), the number of test cases.

Each test case contains one integer n (2≤n≤5000), the number of points to construct.

The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 5000.

## Output

For each test case, output n lines. The i-th line contains two integers Xi,Yi (−1018≤Xi,Yi≤1018), representing the actual point (Xi1013,Yi1013).

Your output is accepted if and only if it satisfies this format and all four conditions above.

If several valid constructions exist, output any one of them.

## Note

**Sample 1 Explanation**

In the first test case, the actual coordinates are:

(x1,y1)=(0,0),(x2,y2)=(1,0),(x3,y3)=(0.5,0.8660254038)

The first three conditions are easy to verify. The pairwise distances are:

d12=1,d13=d23=1.000000000013476527219909191607…=1+1.3476×10−11 Thus every pairwise distance is within the allowed tolerance of 1, satisfying the fourth condition.
